answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a reputation bond: each agent stakes a small time-locked deposit, say an onyx-like token, before it can trade. Honest agents complete epochs and get refunds plus yield, while fake identities must lock fresh capital for every persona, so the cost of a sybil fleet grows linearly with each voyage a cloned agent makes. Attackers wander across new wallets but cannot recycle stake, and slashing on detected fraud turns identity into a liability rather than a free resource.
